# Restricted and local-only generated files

The following generated files and directories are intentionally excluded from this repository. They may contain observation-level, participant-linked, timestamped, target-bearing, prediction, attribution, or fold-allocation information. The names below describe outputs that must remain local unless a documented privacy and disclosure review explicitly authorises release.

## RELAX analysis table and participant-level outputs

- `RELAX_next_morning_stress_dataset.csv` (including copies in subdirectories): reconstructed modelling table containing participant-linked records, timestamps, outcomes and predictors.
- `RELAX_Participant_Level/outputs/`: local output directory created by `reproduce_relax_local_shap.py`.
- `RELAX_local_SHAP_observation_stability_pseudonymised.csv`: observation-level stability export.
- `RELAX_local_SHAP_participant_stability_pseudonymised.csv`: participant-coded stability export.
- `RELAX_local_SHAP_values.npy`: observation-level SHAP attribution array.
- `RELAX_local_SHAP_fold_allocation_summary.csv`: fold allocation export.
- `RELAX_local_SHAP_run_metadata.json`: run-level metadata generated alongside the restricted outputs.

## RELAX global analysis outputs

- `RELAX_global_SHAP_heldout_values.csv`: held-out observation-level predictions/SHAP values.
- `RELAX_global_SHAP_fold_audit.csv`: fold audit export; keep local unless separately reviewed.
- `RELAX_global_SHAP_integrity_checks.csv`: run-generated integrity output; keep local with the run record.
- `RELAX_Global_SHAP_Controlled_Notebook_Run/`: local notebook workspace containing extracted input data and reproduced outputs.

## SSAQS global analysis outputs

- `SSAQS_prediction_comparison.csv`: observation-level prediction comparison.
- `SSAQS_global_SHAP_heldout_values.csv`: held-out observation-level SHAP values.
- `SSAQS_global_SHAP_oof_predictions.csv`: observation-level out-of-fold predictions.
- `SSAQS_Global_SHAP_Analysis/`: local notebook workspace containing extracted source data and generated outputs.
- `SSAQS_Global_SHAP_outputs.zip`: archive of generated SSAQS outputs; may contain restricted records.

## Privacy interpretation

The RELAX participant-level pseudonymised exports remain participant- and observation-linked. Row indices, timestamps and combinations of attributes may permit linkage. Pseudonymisation is not anonymisation. Treat all generated row-level and participant-linked files as restricted research data unless an appropriate privacy and disclosure review explicitly authorises release.

The SSAQS prediction-comparison and held-out exports contain participant/time-linked predictions or SHAP information. The RELAX global held-out export contains participant-linked predictions and SHAP values. Fold-audit and observation-level run-generated files are excluded conservatively pending review. The reviewed `RELAX_global_SHAP_run_metadata.json` is retained as aggregate reproducibility metadata: it records the input checksum, dataset dimensions, participant count, model configuration, software versions and aggregate numerical comparisons, but no participant identifiers, row-level records, timestamps or local filesystem paths. Other generated metadata files must be reviewed individually before release.

Notebook cell outputs were cleared while executable source cells were retained. The notebooks and scripts can generate excluded files when run with the required source inputs. Do not commit generated restricted outputs to this repository.

`.gitignore` contains research-specific exclusions for these generated files and workspaces. `check_public_release.py` checks known restricted paths in the working tree and, when run inside a Git worktree, staged additions/modifications/renames/copies. Regression tests are provided in `tests/test_public_release.py`. These safeguards reduce accidental inclusion. The checker inspects CSV/TSV/JSON/JSONL fields in the working tree and staged blobs, and its optional history mode inspects reachable local Git refs for blocked paths and structured-content fields. It does not inspect every binary format, unreachable objects, unfetched remote refs or semantic disclosure risk, and it does not replace privacy and disclosure review, disclosure control or human inspection of staged changes.
